candidates.title: Mechanics
candidates.thesis: Everything the player does, read out of the engine rather than out of the old design doc.

candidates.title: ARM - HALT
candidates.thesis: Plant a halt trap on open junctions on the enemy board. When their signal claims the node, **they lose a full turn**.

candidates.title: ARM - SIPHON
candidates.thesis: Plant a siphon trap on open junctions on the enemy board. When it fires, RAM **drains from their next turn into yours**.

candidates.title: ATTACK
candidates.thesis: The only program that reaches the **enemy** board. 1 RAM, once per turn.

candidates.title: Augment drafts
candidates.thesis: One draft per **cleared ticket**. Three tickets a day, so a clean day banks three picks.

candidates.title: CHEAP SHOT
candidates.thesis: Reads `econ.attacksCast`. Worth exactly 1 RAM per dive, which sounds small and is not: an opening turn with a free [[redirect]] converts directly into rotations, and opening tempo is what the [[the-board]] generator is calibrated around.

candidates.title: CLAMP DRIVER
candidates.thesis: The description string is built from `LOCK_ROUNDS`, so the copy cannot drift from the constant.

candidates.title: CLEAN RUN
candidates.thesis: Two payouts, both rewarding precision:

candidates.title: DARKNET RATE
candidates.thesis: The copy is careful to say what the discount does **not** buy: it does not make the roll visible and it does not open any other payment. [[ruling-09-darknet]] keeps the dealer permanently anonymous, so a relationship discount is as far as the fiction allows.

candidates.title: DEEP SIPHON
candidates.thesis: Stacks on `SIPHON_STEAL`, so at ATTACK tier 3 a siphon moves 5 RAM.

candidates.title: ECHO TAP
candidates.thesis: Fires for either trap kind, so it works with [[arm-halt]] and [[arm-siphon]] both. Arrives through `drainNext` as a negative, like [[cascades-and-surge|cascade RAM]].

candidates.title: FIRST FAULT
candidates.thesis: In `finishDuel`:

candidates.title: HALT DRIVER
candidates.thesis: Unlocks the mode; does not switch to it. Select it in [[loadout-cfg]].

candidates.title: HOT BOOT
candidates.thesis: Like [[cheap-shot]], a one-RAM effect that buys opening tempo. The `minPd` floor in [[difficulty-dials|DayConfig]] exists partly because boosts like this can otherwise let an opening burst close a short board outright.

candidates.title: JAM ANCHOR
candidates.thesis: A lock effect without spending [[defend]]. The twist and the clamp in one 1 RAM cast, which is the strongest single tempo play available to a REDIRECT build.

candidates.title: LONG ARMS
candidates.thesis: The cascade-scaling boost. Reach 2 lets you hold a chain; reach 4 lets you hold a much longer one, which moves you up the `cascadeRam` curve. See [[reach-and-placement]].

candidates.title: OVERTIME CLAUSE
candidates.thesis: The fiction is billing, and it is canon: [[ruling-10-overtime-billing]] settled that the shop can bill overtime, which is what makes this an in-world contract term rather than an arbitrary number.

candidates.title: SIPHON DRIVER
candidates.thesis: Steal scales with ATTACK tier: 2, 3, 4 RAM. See [[program-tiers]].

candidates.title: SPLICE REFUND
candidates.thesis: Gated by `{ kind: "pouch" }`, the only non-augment requirement in the system: the pouch must hold at least one piece **at roll time**. So the draft will not offer it to a player with an empty pouch, even though they might fill it later.

candidates.title: SWEEP CREDIT
candidates.thesis: At DEFEND tier 3 against a trap-heavy board, a purge that clears 3 traps refunds 3 RAM against a 1 RAM cast, so it is RAM positive.

candidates.title: TAP LINE
candidates.thesis: Stored as `DuelState.routeTrace: { round, cells }`, cleared each round.

candidates.title: TRIPWIRE
candidates.thesis: The forfeited turn plus a drain on the turn after it. This is the `drain` field on the trap record. See [[traps-and-telegraphs]].

candidates.title: WARD DRIVER
candidates.thesis: Radius scales with DEFEND tier: 1, 2, 3. See [[program-tiers]].

candidates.title: Augments
candidates.thesis: Two kinds. Configs unlock a mode on a program; boosts change a rule.

candidates.title: Boost bays
candidates.thesis: BOOST_SLOTS_BASE = 3

candidates.title: Built and power
candidates.thesis: Two layers per board. Keeping them apart is the whole design.

candidates.title: Cascades and surge
candidates.thesis: The signature moment. Hold a long chain aligned behind one unturned junction, then flip that junction and light all of it at once.

candidates.title: Credits
candidates.thesis: The run currency. Earned by clearing tickets, spent at night.

candidates.title: Death, lives and run end
candidates.thesis: Deliberately. There is no life counter, no continues, no revives, and no mid-run checkpoint. A run either reaches day 10 or it ends.

candidates.title: DEFEND
candidates.thesis: Acts on **your own** board. 1 RAM, once per turn.

candidates.title: Difficulty dials
candidates.thesis: Three knobs govern how hard the machine is. Only two of them are load-bearing.

candidates.title: Economy
candidates.thesis: Three currencies, on three different clocks.

candidates.title: Job pay and billing
candidates.thesis: jobPay(tier)          = 40 + 25 * tier

candidates.title: LOCK
candidates.thesis: Freeze junctions for **2 rounds** (`LOCK_ROUNDS`). Nothing rotates or redirects them.

candidates.title: Neural Strain
candidates.thesis: The run's health bar. It is the only thing that ends a run early.

candidates.title: Opponent AI
candidates.thesis: The intrusion is a scripted opponent, not a search. It runs the same Dijkstra you do, on its own board, and decides each turn whether to race or to interfere.

candidates.title: Patch pieces
candidates.thesis: Single-use shaped fills. A piece is a **4-bit arm mask with its orientation baked in**: it is never rotatable, in hand or on the board.

candidates.title: Player character
candidates.thesis: The son. Unnamed, never pictured, never speaks in the third person.

candidates.title: Player inventory
candidates.thesis: Three containers, all capped, all emptied at run end.

candidates.title: Player metrics
candidates.thesis: Every number attached to the player, and where it lives.

candidates.title: Player skills
candidates.thesis: The skill system, such as it is. There are no skill trees, no XP and no levels.

candidates.title: Program tiers
candidates.thesis: Width is targets per cast: nodes redirected, traps planted, traps cleared, locks placed.

candidates.title: PURGE
candidates.thesis: Disarm revealed traps on your own board. 1, 2 or 3 per cast by `DEFEND_WIDTH`.

candidates.title: RAM
candidates.thesis: The per-turn action budget. RAM is what makes the duel a game of choices rather than a puzzle with one answer.

candidates.title: Reach and placement
candidates.thesis: Reach is how far ahead of your built ground you are allowed to work.

candidates.title: REDIRECT
candidates.thesis: Twist enemy or open junctions a quarter turn, **anywhere on the board, no reach limit**. Cuts power to everything downstream.

candidates.title: Rotation
candidates.thesis: The only movement verb. You twist a junction a quarter turn so its arms line up and signal flows further.

candidates.title: Route cost and par
candidates.thesis: One function prices the entire game.

candidates.title: SCAN
candidates.thesis: Information. 1 RAM, once per turn, acts on your own board.

candidates.title: Scoring and lifetime stats
candidates.thesis: There is no score. Nothing ranks the player and nothing is optimized for points.

candidates.title: Split boards
candidates.thesis: Each side owns a grid. `DuelState.boards` is a `Record<Side, Board>` where `Side = "player" | "opp"`. Yours is `boards.player`, the intrusion's is `boards.opp`.

candidates.title: The board
candidates.thesis: Each side's grid is generated from the run seed, then rejection-sampled until it is fair.

candidates.title: The darknet
candidates.thesis: The gray market. One blind [[patch-pieces|patch piece]], priced by day.

candidates.title: The duel
candidates.thesis: The duel is the combat system. Every dive into a customer's device is one duel against one intrusion. It is turn-based, deterministic from a seed, and it is a race rather than a fight: nobody has hit points.

candidates.title: The kit
candidates.thesis: Every diver, and every intrusion, carries exactly three programs.

candidates.title: The night shop
candidates.thesis: Day close. One free pick, plus anything you can afford.

candidates.title: The pouch
candidates.thesis: Where [[patch-pieces]] are carried. `PATCH_POUCH_MAX = 5`.

candidates.title: The round cap
candidates.thesis: ROUND_CAP = 25

candidates.title: Traps and telegraphs
candidates.thesis: Interference comes in two forms: a mine you walk into later, and a move you can see coming one beat early.

candidates.title: Turn structure
candidates.thesis: One round is one player turn then one opponent turn. `round` is 1-based.

candidates.title: WARD
candidates.thesis: Ward a junction and everything within a Manhattan radius of it for **2 rounds** (`WARD_ROUNDS`).

candidates.title: Win conditions
candidates.thesis: Three outcomes. That is the complete list.

candidates.title: Content
candidates.thesis: Everything authored: the arc, the roster, the artifacts, the scenes.

candidates.title: Aldous Wick
candidates.thesis: The only customer spanning three tiers, so he recurs across the arc at rising difficulty. A halt-trap job: the heaviest tempo punishment in the game, and the strongest argument for [[scan]] first.

candidates.title: Bram Hollander
candidates.thesis: A clamp job. Junctions you need freeze solid for two rounds, which is the most frustrating denial in the game if you have no answer, and trivial if you do.

candidates.title: Casimir Bell
candidates.thesis: Not yet ruled. **Invent nothing without a ruling.**

candidates.title: Dex Marlowe
candidates.thesis: The mid-tier redirect job. Same routine as [[sable-okonkwo]] one band up, so it is a natural difficulty check: the player who cleared Sable comfortably meets the same verb against a wider cast.

candidates.title: Emeric Snow
candidates.thesis: Not yet ruled. **Invent nothing without a ruling.**

candidates.title: Ines Calloway
candidates.thesis: Not yet ruled. **Invent nothing without a ruling.**

candidates.title: June Aksoy
candidates.thesis: Not yet ruled. **Invent nothing without a ruling.**

candidates.title: Juno Vex
candidates.thesis: An early-tier siphon job, so it is often a player's first encounter with traps that steal [[ram]] rather than deny tempo. The Analyze tell will say so: "It wants your RAM more than your route. Scan early."

candidates.title: Noor Behzadi
candidates.thesis: Not yet ruled. **Invent nothing without a ruling.**

candidates.title: Sable Okonkwo
candidates.thesis: A redirect job at low tier: the cleanest introduction to the interference economy, because the damage is visible (your chain goes dark) and the counter is obvious (twist it back, and notice what it cost).

candidates.title: Vera Stanek
candidates.thesis: Not yet ruled. **Invent nothing without a ruling.**

candidates.title: Wren Tallis
candidates.thesis: A low-tier ward job, which is unusual: warding is prevention, so the intrusion is not attacking so much as refusing to be attacked. Your traps will not land and your redirects will bounce inside the bubble.

candidates.title: Customers
candidates.thesis: Twelve regulars. Every job is an intrusion in a machine somebody loves.

candidates.title: Day 1
candidates.thesis: The gentlest configuration in the game. **horizon 0** means the machine does no cut scoring at all: it simply races its own board and never reaches across to interfere. The player meets the race before they meet the duel.

candidates.title: Day 10 - the finale
candidates.thesis: No job board. The back room settles up.

candidates.title: Day 2
candidates.thesis: The day line does the teaching the interface does not: **strain carries over**. It is the first statement that the run is a resource arc rather than a series of independent jobs.

candidates.title: Day 3
candidates.thesis: Three things change together: the grid grows, `headStart` arrives, and the patch drop rate falls by a third.

candidates.title: Day 4
candidates.thesis: The machine now also scores by **how much of the player's live grid goes dark**. Cuts stop being about route cost alone and start being about tempo damage.

candidates.title: Day 5
candidates.thesis: The first day with a floor on the player's opening route cost. By day 5 a kitted player has enough boosts, banked [[cascades-and-surge|cascade]] RAM and [[patch-pieces|pieces]] that an opening burst could otherwise close a short board outright. `minPd` stops the generator handing out a board that can be solved on turn one.

candidates.title: Day 6
candidates.thesis: First day where all three tickets are tier 3.

candidates.title: Day 7
candidates.thesis: First tier 4 ticket, which means an opponent carrying two attack modes and two defend modes, casting two targets wide.

candidates.title: Day 8
candidates.thesis: The machine reaches full intelligence. It now:

candidates.title: Day 9
candidates.thesis: Every curve is at its working-day extreme: the largest head start, the tightest par margin, the most slag, the fewest drops, and the first **tier 5** ticket.

candidates.title: Intrusions
candidates.thesis: Clearing one is not deleting static code. It fights back. That is why every repair is a dive, and why every shop ticket is an intrusion job.

candidates.title: THE BACK ROOM
candidates.thesis: The player queried the shop's ticketing system for the tower and found nothing:

candidates.title: FINAL NOTICE
candidates.thesis: Meridian Neurocare, unpaid, one of **eleven**. The father had medical debt bigger than a year of shop income, and hid it.

candidates.title: THE DIAGNOSIS
candidates.thesis: NF-3 neurofilament degradation, **stage three**. 9,000+ logged dive hours.

candidates.title: ANOTHER FAILED RUN
candidates.thesis: The tower's own record of the opening dive. The machine did not fight. **It graded him and shut the door.**

candidates.title: IT IS GRADING ME
candidates.thesis: Eight dives of the tower's own telemetry, aggregated. The pattern is unmistakable: it went easy when he was weak, and it hardened exactly as fast as he improved.

candidates.title: NO TICKETS
candidates.thesis: Cross-referenced against the shop's ledger: **no client ever existed**. The hours, the strain and the death were for something he was building in secret, on an installment plan.

candidates.title: PATCH
candidates.thesis: The name, the reason for it, and the whole truth.

candidates.title: RECEIPTS
candidates.thesis: Strain suppressants. Weekly. Cash. **Six years.** Climbing dosage.

candidates.title: SOLDER SMOKE
candidates.thesis: The soldering lesson. [[dad]] at the bench with a child.

candidates.title: THE WILL
candidates.thesis: The inheritance, and the division of the shop: counter to [[rhea]], bench to [[the-player]].

candidates.title: The finale encounter
candidates.thesis: The game's only boss, and it is deliberately not a boss.

candidates.title: The shop
candidates.thesis: A family computer repair shop, inherited jointly by the two kids on [[dad]]'s death, per the will taped inside the register.

candidates.title: The ten-day arc
candidates.thesis: Nine working days of three tickets each, then day 10.

candidates.title: World overview
candidates.thesis: Near-future cyberpunk city, **seen entirely from inside one repair shop**.

candidates.title: Game controls
candidates.thesis: Targeting is click-to-select, and `badTargetCount` and `illegalTarget` are refusal reasons the command gate returns, so partial target selection is a real state. See [[turn-structure]].

candidates.title: KP/OS
candidates.thesis: The shop terminal's retro pixel desktop. **The game does not have an interface. The interface is the game.**

candidates.title: Music and sound
candidates.thesis: An **sfxr preset palette rendered to buffers on demand**, plus a small additive synth for stingers, plus a music manager for the generated beds.

candidates.title: Player options
candidates.thesis: A short list, deliberately. Everything here is either accessibility or taste.

candidates.title: Title and start screen
candidates.thesis: There is no title screen. There is a **boot sequence**.

candidates.title: BACKROOM.LCK
candidates.thesis: The `finalePre` screen of [[shopfront-exe]]

candidates.title: DAD.LOG (the window)
candidates.thesis: The read-only archive reader over DAD.VOL. Integrated 2026-07-29.

candidates.title: DARKNET.LNK
candidates.thesis: The gray-market CLI. Night phase only. `notched: true` chrome.

candidates.title: DIVE.EXE
candidates.thesis: Full-screen · `components/game/duel.tsx`

candidates.title: INBOX
candidates.thesis: The job board and the CUSTOMER.REC card. Fronts the day loop and launches the dive.

candidates.title: LEDGER.LOG
candidates.thesis: The accounting terminal. There is no score; there are books.

candidates.title: LOADOUT.CFG
candidates.thesis: The kit. **The v3 reference implementation**, and the panel every other surface is built against.

candidates.title: MANUAL.TXT
candidates.thesis: The reference. Five tabs, page-flip navigation: **DIVE · KIT · PATCHES · AUGMENTS · BAYS**.

candidates.title: NIGHT.SYS
candidates.thesis: The `upgrade` screen of [[shopfront-exe]] · `windows/night.tsx`

candidates.title: REPAIR.LOG
candidates.thesis: The post-dive result, **read as a transaction**.

candidates.title: SHOPFRONT.EXE
candidates.thesis: Because they are the same object at different times of day: the story surface. A separate window per story state would put five icons on the desktop for one thing that is never open twice at once.

candidates.title: SOLDER.BAY
candidates.thesis: The patch-piece bench. Crafting lives here and nowhere else.

candidates.title: Teaching
candidates.thesis: How the player learns the game. Owned by the [[tutorial-agent]], enforced by a build-failing test.

candidates.title: Coachmarks
candidates.thesis: One-time callouts. **A coachmark is a rule you need once.**

candidates.title: Mechanic coverage
candidates.thesis: The inventory of everything a player must understand, and how each one is covered.

candidates.title: Placement bias order
candidates.thesis: The most reusable thing the teaching ledger contains. **Five tiers, and you take the lowest one that works.**

candidates.title: Standing lessons
candidates.thesis: Craft rules extracted from thirteen dated cycle retrospectives in `tutorial/ledger.md`. The retrospectives stay there; the lessons belong here, because they are reusable and their dates are not.

candidates.title: Teaching system
candidates.thesis: 1. **Every mechanic resolves to a moment or a written waiver.** Enforced by `teach-sim.ts`, which exits 1 and names the gap.

candidates.title: Teaching tips
candidates.thesis: Persistent hover explainers. **A tip is reference you want again.**

candidates.title: Teaching waivers
candidates.thesis: A waiver is a **written decision not to teach something**, with a reason. **14 of the 39** inventory entries carry one, against 25 taught (`teach-sim.ts`, 2026-08-05).

candidates.title: The tutorial
candidates.thesis: The opening dive. **Unwinnable by construction**, and it must prove it 200 times before any deploy.

candidates.title: Tutorial beats
candidates.thesis: Beats are how the tutorial teaches, because coachmarks are gated off day 0 by `notBeforeDay: 1`. See [[teaching-system]].
